issues.detail: Hebrew וּבְצַלְעִי (from צלע, 'limping/maimed ones') is rendered as '我的肋骨' (my ribs), which is a different meaning. The Hebrew refers to 'maimed/limping people' (likely enemies), not anatomical ribs.

Hebrew נֵכִים (from נכה, 'stricken/smitten ones') is rendered as '敵人' (enemies), which is an interpretive addition; the Hebrew says 'stricken ones' (likely meaning 'wretches' or 'afflicted'), not explicitly 'enemies'.
